name: Mizzah
overview: Mizzah was a male Edomite, recognized as the son of Reuel and a chief of Edom. His leadership role among the Edomites marks him as a notable figure within this tribe. Scripture identifies him specifically in Genesis 36:13 and 36:17 without additional personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Mizzah means "terror" and is a proper name not given directly by God. This name is recorded in Genesis 36:13, reflecting the Hebrew meaning associated with him.
familyAndRelationships: Mizzah is recorded as the son of Reuel according to Genesis 36:13. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not provide further family connections for him.
scriptureSignificance: Mizzah's significance lies in his status as a chief of Edom and as a descendant of Reuel, situating him within the genealogical and leadership framework of the Edomite people. His mention in Genesis 36 highlights the organization and notable figures within Edom, contributing to the biblical record of the descendants of Esau.
